task: Cycle 6 C6-02: Blackwell small-shape NVFP4 quantizer fusion, fused cuBLASLt alpha and wide cross-mix latency against the C6-01 perplexities

kernel_parity.reference: micro_rotated_ptq rotation (FP32) + nvfp4_encode + pack_e2m1 + to_blocked (nb.quantize_activation_ref); the packed-table cases also compare the layer output with the C5-03 NVFP4Linear bit for bit

part_a.design: Williams-balanced orders over all methods; CUDA events, mean of `iters` flushed samples per round (raw per-call times in event_samples_ms), 4x L2 flush before every sample; median over rounds. `wall_ms`: host clock between synchronizes. c5_03_* is nvfp4_inference_blackwell (pinned bytes) with torch._scaled_mm_v2; c6_02_* is nvfp4_small_shape_blackwell (FastNVFP4Linear sharing the same NVFP4 weights) with the direct cuBLASLt call; both allocate their buffers per call. Large inputs (fs.DELEGATE_FROM, fs.DELEGATE_MIN_K per rotation) are delegated to the C5-03 path by design.

part_b.design: Profiler traces of one call (CPU aten ops, CUDA kernels); the direct cuBLASLt call writes into a NaN-filled output (beta = 0 must not read C) and is compared bit for bit with nvfp4_scaled_mm_public for every shape, rotation and output dtype; every heuristic algorithm (with its own workspace when it needs one) is checked bit for bit and timed as a CUDA graph (4x L2 flush).

part_c.design: random-init BF16 weights and tokens; every block linear (qkv, out, gate, up, down) replaced by an RTN NVFP4 layer. bf16_graph: one CUDA graph of the eager BF16 forward; bf16_compiled: torch.compile(model) with default Inductor settings under inference mode, 3 warm-up calls, timed eagerly (the C5-03 primary BF16 comparator). Variants: c5_03_* nvfp4_inference_blackwell, c6_02_* FastNVFP4Linear on the same weights. Wide families: c6_01_* = rotated_qat.CrossInput (FP32 PyTorch cross-block mix) over the C5-03 layer (the C6-01 hardware path), c6_02_crossinput_* the same over FastNVFP4Linear, c6_02_fused_* FastCrossInput (exact=False: one Triton cross-mix kernel, a latency path whose logits parity is measured per model). One CUDA graph per forward (shared memory pool), every method in one Williams-balanced session, 4x L2 flush. Embedding, norms, attention and the tied head stay BF16. compiled_bf16_trained_eval: the compiled BF16 forward on the six pinned trained C6-01 checkpoints (full test split).

caveats: nvfp4_inference_blackwell.py (C5-03) is unchanged: the C5-03 and C6-01 validators pin its bytes, so the C6-02 fast path is the separate module nvfp4_small_shape_blackwell (drop-in, bit-identical operands and outputs).

Part A: C6-02 beats BF16 cuBLAS in 31/32 CUDA-graph cells; trailing cells: [[1024, 512, 1408, 'bfly_b16']]; non-delegated cells slower than C5-03: none. Each cell is one Williams-balanced session and the GPU also drives the desktop: the timing-anomaly caveat lists every cell whose rounds a stall affected.

Timing anomalies: 0 stall-affected cells (relative IQR of round means above 0.15 in Part A or 0.05 in Part C, or 5+ rounds with an event above 3x the event median and 0.100 ms). Maximum relative IQR: Part A 0.0374, Part C 0.0095.

Large inputs use the C5-03 quantizer and torch._scaled_mm_v2 by design (fs.delegated: none from 2^23 elements, the butterfly from 2^21 elements with K >= 2048, never hadamard_b16): there the DRAM-bound C5-03 2D tiles match or beat the C6-02 kernels (c6_02_no_delegate ablation at 2048 x 8192; the limits come from pre-run sweeps recorded in the module). Delegated cells run the same code as C5-03: [[1024, 768, 2048, 'bfly_b16'], [1024, 4096, 4096, 'bfly_b16'], [2048, 8192, 8192, 'none'], [2048, 8192, 8192, 'bfly_b16']]; their C5-03/C6-02 differences are session noise.

Part B: the elementwise kernel is aten::mul of the two FP32 tensor scales inside torch._scaled_mm_v2; the C6-02 quantizer writes alpha = global_scale * w_global (one rounded FP32 product, the same value) and the GEMM calls cublasLtMatmul with PyTorch's descriptor (1 MiB heuristic limit, device pointer mode). Equality with nvfp4_scaled_mm_public is measured bit for bit, not derived; it holds for the cuBLASLt build of this torch wheel. The direct call runs through ctypes (host cost in eager mode).

Part C models use random weights: latency does not depend on the weight values. The NLL axis of the Pareto comes from the C6-01 three-seed test means (pinned C6-01 result) for the quantized methods and bf16_graph, and from this run's compiled BF16 scoring of the same six trained checkpoints for bf16_compiled.

Two BF16 references: bf16_graph (a CUDA graph of the eager forward: launch overhead removed, no fusion) and bf16_compiled (torch.compile default Inductor, timed eagerly in the same session: fused elementwise work). bf16_compiled is the primary reference, as in C5-03. Medians: 50m graph 14.551 ms, compiled 11.773 ms; 120m graph 12.844 ms, compiled 10.794 ms; w2048_6l graph 17.632 ms, compiled 16.688 ms.

Pareto 50m (trained compiled BF16 test NLL 5.382034, three seeds; C6-01 BF16 5.382032): compiled BF16 dominates all 3 wide paths (each is slower and has a higher test NLL). Primary frontier (with bf16_compiled): ['hadamard_b16_gptq_static', 'gptq', 'adaptive_butterfly_b16_gptq', 'bf16_compiled', 'bf16_graph']; frontier against bf16_graph only: ['hadamard_b16_gptq_static', 'gptq', 'adaptive_butterfly_b16_gptq', 'cross_full_butterfly_b16_gptq', 'bf16_graph'].

Pareto 120m (trained compiled BF16 test NLL 4.624276, three seeds; C6-01 BF16 4.624285): compiled BF16 dominates none of the wide paths; ['kron_hadamard_full_gptq', 'cross_full_butterfly_b16_gptq'] run faster than compiled BF16, and ['kron_hadamard_full_gptq', 'cross_full_butterfly_b16_gptq'] stay on the primary frontier. Primary frontier (with bf16_compiled): ['hadamard_b16_gptq_static', 'kron_hadamard_full_gptq', 'cross_full_butterfly_b16_gptq', 'bf16_compiled']; frontier against bf16_graph only: ['hadamard_b16_gptq_static', 'kron_hadamard_full_gptq', 'cross_full_butterfly_b16_gptq', 'bf16_graph'].

The fused cross-mix (FastCrossInput, exact=False) follows the two-half FMA order of the cuBLAS gemmSN kernels; where cuBLAS picks another kernel single mixed FP32 values differ by rounding (about 1e-6), which can flip packed FP4 codes. Later blocks amplify such flips, so a small mixed-value difference does not bound the logits error. FastCrossInput(exact=True) runs the reference mix bit for bit at any shape.

Fused cross-mix fidelity, 50m: hadamard_b64 logits bit-identical to the C6-01 path on these weights (60/60 layers with bit-identical mixed values); kron_hadamard_full logits bit-identical to the C6-01 path on these weights (60/60 layers with bit-identical mixed values); cross_full_butterfly_b16 logits bit-identical to the C6-01 path on these weights (60/60 layers with bit-identical mixed values). Scope: the C6-01 test NLL is assigned to the fused paths that match bit for bit; the timing tokens are not the test windows, so this is a random-weight parity check, not a trained-weight proof.

Fused cross-mix fidelity, 120m: hadamard_b64 logits bit-identical to the C6-01 path on these weights (60/60 layers with bit-identical mixed values); kron_hadamard_full logits bit-identical to the C6-01 path on these weights (48/60 layers with bit-identical mixed values); cross_full_butterfly_b16 logits bit-identical to the C6-01 path on these weights (48/60 layers with bit-identical mixed values). Scope: the C6-01 test NLL is assigned to the fused paths that match bit for bit; the timing tokens are not the test windows, so this is a random-weight parity check, not a trained-weight proof.

Fused cross-mix fidelity, w2048_6l: hadamard_b64 logits bit-identical to the C6-01 path on these weights (30/30 layers with bit-identical mixed values); kron_hadamard_full latency only, not exact (102127503 logits differ, relative L2 0.2091; no trained NLL qualification); cross_full_butterfly_b16 latency only, not exact (102294865 logits differ, relative L2 0.2533; no trained NLL qualification). Scope: no C6-01 trained cell exists for this model: latency only.
Every wide-family linear computes its own cross-mix as in the C6-01 hardware path (gate and up mix the same input twice); sharing it would be a further model-level change, not measured here.
The butterfly coefficients of FastNVFP4Linear live in a non-persistent (16, G, 4) buffer derived from the (cos, sin) tables; the public quantize_activation keeps the (G, 4, 8) table API.

The delegation limits (fs.DELEGATE_FROM, fs.DELEGATE_MIN_K) were changed after the first canonical attempt, from RTX 5080 sweeps on shapes that overlap this grid: they are performance-informed routing for the measured shapes. The zero count of non-delegated regressions does not show a uniformly faster native quantizer and does not predict the crossover on unseen shapes.
